occultation: 1. (Astron.) The hiding of a heavenly body from sight by the intervention of some other of the heavenly bodies; -- applied especially to eclipses of stars and planets by the moon, and to the eclipses of satellites of planets by their primaries. 2. Fig.: The state of being occult. The reappearance of such an author after those long periods of occultation. Jeffrey.
octant: 1. (Geom.) The eighth part of a circle; an arc of 45 degrees. 2. (Astron. & Astrol.) The position or aspect of a heavenly body, as the moon or a planet, when half way between conjunction, or opposition, and quadrature, or distant from another body 45 degrees. 3.
occursion: A meeting; a clash; a collision. (old) Boyle.
occultism: A certain Oriental system of theosophy. A. P. Sinnett.
octaemeron: A fast of eight days before a great festival. Shipley.
octosyllabical: Consisting of or containing eight syllables.
oceanus: The god of the great outer sea, or the river which was believed to flow around the whole earth.
ochreated: 1. Wearing or furnished with an ochrea or legging; wearing boots; booted. A scholar undertook...to address himself ochreated unto the vice chancellor. Fuller. 2. (Bot.) Provided with ochrea, or sheathformed stipules, as the rhubarb, yellow dock, and knotgrass.
octandrian: Of or pertaining to the Octandria; having eight distinct stamens.
octosyllable: Octosyllabic. | A word of eight syllables.
ocellated: 1. Resembling an eye. 2. Marked with eyelike spots of color; as, the ocellated blenny. Ocellated turkey (Zoöl.), the wild turkey of Central America (Meleagris ocellata).
octoate: A salt of an octoic acid; a caprylate.
octagonal: Having eight sides and eight angles.
ochreate: 1. Wearing or furnished with an ochrea or legging; wearing boots; booted. A scholar undertook...to address himself ochreated unto the vice chancellor. Fuller. 2. (Bot.) Provided with ochrea, or sheathformed stipules, as the rhubarb, yellow dock, and knotgrass.
occupant: 1. One who occupies, or takes possession; one who has the actual use or possession, or is in possession, of a thing. Note: This word, in law, sometimes signifies one who takes the first possession of a thing that has no owner. 2. A prostitute. (old) Marston.
octo: A combining form meaning eight; as in octodecimal, octodecimal, octolocular.
occupancy: The act of taking or holding possession; possession; occupation. Title by occupancy (Law), a right of property acquired by taking the first possession of a thing, or possession of a thing which belonged to nobody, and appropriating it. Blackstone. Kent.
octroi: 1. A privilege granted by the sovereign authority, as the exclusive right of trade granted to a guild or society; a concession. 2. A tax levied in money or kind at the gate of a French city on articles brought within the walls. [Written also octroy.]
ocean: 1. The whole body of salt water which covers more than three fifths of the surface of the globe; -- called also the sea, or great sea. Like the odor of brine from the ocean Comes the thought of other… | Of or pertaining to the main or great sea; as, the ocean waves; an ocean stream. Milton.
occurrence: 1. A coming or happening; as, the occurence of a railway collision. Voyages detain the mind by the perpetual occurrence and expectation of something new. I. Watts. 2. Any incident or event; esp., one which happens without being designed or expected; as, an unusual occurrence, or the ordinary occurrences of life. All the occurrence of my fortune. Shak. Syn. -- See Event.
oculate: 1. Furnished with eyes. 2. Having spots or holes resembling eyes; ocellated.
occupy: 1. To take or hold possession of; to hold or keep for use; to possess. Woe occupieth the fine [/end] of our gladness. Chaucer. The better apartments were already occupied. W. Irving . 2. | 1. To hold possession; to be an occupant. "Occupy till I come." Luke xix. 13. 2. To follow business; to traffic.
oculus: 1. An eye; (Bot.) a leaf bud. 2. (Arch.) A round window, usually a small one.
octave: 1. The eighth day after a church festival, the festival day being included; also, the week following a church festival. "The octaves of Easter." Jer. Taylor. 2. (Mus.) (a) The eighth tone in the… | Consisting of eight; eight. Dryden.
occasioner: One who, or that which, occasions, causes, or produces. Bp. Sanderson.
oculiform: In the form of an eye; resembling an eye; as, an oculiform pebble.
octamerous: Having the parts in eights; as, an octamerous flower; octamerous mesenteries in polyps.
occlude: 1. To shut up; to close. Sir T. Browne. 2. (Chem.) To take in and retain; to absorb; -- said especially with respect to gases; as iron, platinum, and palladium occlude large volumes of hydrogen.
ocarina: A kind of small simple wind instrument.
octylic: Pertaining to, derived from, or containing, octyl; as, octylic ether.
octogenary: Of eighty years of age. "Being then octogenary." Aubrey.
ocelot: An American feline carnivore (Felis pardalis). It ranges from the Southwestern United States to Patagonia. It is covered with blackish ocellated spots and blotches, which are variously arranged. The ground color varies from reddish gray to tawny yellow.
oculinacea: A suborder of corals including many reef-building species, having round, starlike calicles.
octosyllabic: Consisting of or containing eight syllables.
ock: A suffix used to form diminutives; as, bullock, hillock.
octylene: Any one of a series of metameric hydrocarbons (C8H16) of the ethylene series. In general they are combustible, colorless liquids.
occrustate: To incrust; to harden. (old) Dr. H. More.
octopoda: (a) Same as Octocerata. (b) Same as Arachnida.
octoyl: A hypothetical radical (C8H15O), regarded as the essential residue of octoic acid.
octane: Any one of a group of metametric hydrocarcons (C8H18) of the methane series. The most important is a colorless, volatile, inflammable liquid, found in petroleum, and a constituent of benzene or ligroin.
octoroon: The offspring of a quadroon and a white person; a mestee.
octyl: A hypothetical hydrocarbon radical regarded as an essential residue of octane, and as entering into its derivatives; as, octyl alcohol.
occipital: Of or pertaining to the occiput, or back part of the head, or to the occipital bone. Occipital bone (Anat.), the bone which forms the posterior segment of the skull and surrounds the great foramen by which the spinal cord leaves the cranium. In the higher vertebrates it is usually composed of four bones, which become consolidated in the adult.
occultness: State or quality of being occult.
octachord: An instrument of eight strings; a system of eight tones. [Also written octochord.]
ochreous: Of or pertaining to ocher; containing or resembling ocher; as, ocherous matter; ocherous soil.
occident: The part of the horizon where the sun last appears in the evening; that part of the earth towards the sunset; the west; -- opposed to orient. Specifically, in former times, Europe as opposed to Asia; now, also, the Western hemisphere. Chaucer. I may wander from east to occident. Shak.
occasionalism: The system of occasional causes; -- a name given to certain theories of the Cartesian school of philosophers, as to the intervention of the First Cause, by which they account for the apparent reciprocal action of the soul and the body.
occipito: A combining form denoting relation to, or situation near, the occiput; as, occipito-axial; occipito-mastoid.
octoic: Pertaining to, derived from, or resembling, octane; -- used specifically, to designate any one of a group of acids, the most important of which is called caprylic acid.
octahedrite: Titanium dioxide occurring in acute octahedral crystals.
oculonasal: Of or pertaining to the region of the eye and the nose; as, the oculonasal, or nasal, nerve, one of the branches of the ophthalmic.
octonary: Of or pertaining to the number eight. Dr. H. More.
ochrea: 1. (Antiq.) A greave or legging. 2. (Bot.) A kind of sheath formed by two stipules united round a stem.
octameter: A verse containing eight feet; as, -- Deep'' in|to'' the | dark''ness | peer''ing, | long'' I | stood'' there | wond'''ring, | fear''ing. Poe.
octandrous: Of or pertaining to the Octandria; having eight distinct stamens.
octogynia: A Linnaean order of plants having eight pistils.
occludent: Serving to close; shutting up. -- n. That which closes or shuts up. Sterne.
octagynous: Having eight pistils or styles; octogynous.
octic: Of the eighth degree or order. -- n. (Alg.) A quantic of the eighth degree.
octogild: A pecuniary compensation for an injury, of eight times the value of the thing.
ocher: (a) A impure earthy ore of iron or a ferruginous clay, usually red (hematite) or yellow (limonite), -- used as a pigment in making paints, etc. The name is also applied to clays of other colors. (b) A metallic oxide occurring in earthy form; as, tungstic ocher or tungstite.
ocularly: By the eye, or by actual sight.
octillion: According to the French method of numeration (which method is followed also in the United States) the number expressed by a unit with twenty-seven ciphers annexed. According to the English method, the number expressed by a unit with forty-eight ciphers annexed. See Numeration.
octet: A composition for eight parts, usually for eight solo instruments or voices.
ochlocracy: A form of government by the multitude; a mobocracy. Hare.
ochroleucous: Yellowish white; having a faint tint of dingy yellow. Gray.
occidental: 1. Of, pertaining to, or situated in, the occident, or west; western; -- opposed to oriental; as, occidental climates, or customs; an occidental planet. 2. Possessing inferior hardness, brilliancy, or beauty; -- used of inferior precious stones and gems, because those found in the Orient are generally superior.
occasion: 1. A falling out, happening, or coming to pass; hence, that which falls out or happens; occurrence; incident. The unlooked-for incidents of family history, and its hidden excitements, and its arduous… | To give occasion to; to cause; to produce; to induce; as, to occasion anxiety. South. If we inquire what it is that occasions men to make several combinations of simple ideas into distinct modes.
occurrent: Occurring or happening; hence, incidental; accidental. | 1. One who meets; hence, an adversary. (old) Holland. 2. Anything that happens; an occurrence. (old) These we must meet with in obvious occurrents of the world. Sir T. Browne.
oculated: 1. Furnished with eyes. 2. Having spots or holes resembling eyes; ocellated.
octennial: Happening every eighth year; also, lasting a period of eight years. Johnson. -- Oc*ten"ni*al*ly, adv.
octopede: An animal having eight feet, as a spider.
octahedron: A solid bounded by eight faces. The regular octahedron is contained by eight equal equilateral triangles.
occasive: Of or pertaining to the setting sun; falling; descending; western.
octahedral: Having eight faces or sides; of, pertaining to, or formed in, octahedrons; as, octahedral cleavage. Octahedral borax (Chem.), borax obtained from a saturated solution in octahedral crystals, which contain five molecules of water of crystallization; distinguished from common or prismatic borax. -- Octahedral iron ore (Min.), magnetite.
occamy: An alloy imitating gold or silver. [Written also ochimy, ochymy, etc.]
ocherous: Of or pertaining to ocher; containing or resembling ocher; as, ocherous matter; ocherous soil.
octavalent: Having a valence of eight; capable of being combined with, exchanged for, or compared with, eight atoms of hydrogen; -- said of certain atoms or radicals.
octa: A prefix meaning eight. See Octo-. | A combining form meaning eight; as in octodecimal, octodecimal, octolocular.
occasionality: Quality or state of being occasional; occasional occurrence.
octogenarian: A person eighty years, or more, of age.
octocerata: A suborder of Cephalopoda including Octopus, Argonauta, and allied genera, having eight arms around the head; -- called also Octopoda.
oculist: One skilled in treating diseases of the eye.
oculomotor: Of or pertaining to the movement of the eye; -- applied especially to the common motor nerves (or third pair of cranial nerves) which supply many of the muscles of the orbit. -- n. The oculomotor nerve.
octandria: A Linnæan class of plants, in which the flowers have eight stamens not united to one another or to the pistil.
oceanology: That branch of science which relates to the ocean.
oceanic: 1. Of or pertaining to the ocean; found or formed in or about, or produced by, the ocean; frequenting the ocean, especially mid-ocean. Petrels are the most aërial and oceanic of birds. Darwin. 2. Of or pertaining to Oceania or its inhabitants.
ochlesis: A general morbid condition induced by the crowding together of many persons, esp. sick persons, under one roof. G. Gregory.
ochlocratical: Of or pertaining to ochlocracy; having the form or character of an ochlocracy; mobocratic. -- Och`lo*crat"ic*al*ly, adv.
occulted: 1. Hidden; secret. (old) Shak. 2. (Astron.) Concealed by the intervention of some other heavenly body, as a star by the moon.
occult: Hidden from the eye or the understanding; inviable; secret; concealed; unknown. It is of an occult kind, and is so insensible in its advances as to escape observation. I. Taylor. | To eclipse; to hide from sight.
octateuch: A collection of eight books; especially, the first eight books of the Old Testament.
ocypodian: One of a tribe of crabs which live in holes in the sand along the seashore, and run very rapidly, -- whence the name.
occasional: 1. Of or pertaining to an occasion or to occasions; occuring at times, but not constant, regular, or systematic; made or happening as opportunity requires or admits; casual; incidental; as, occasional remarks, or efforts. The... occasional writing of the present times. Bagehot. 2. Produced by accident; as, the occasional origin of a thing. (old) Sir T. Browne.
october: 1. The tenth month of the year, containing thirty-one days. 2. Ale or cider made in that month. The country gentlemen had a posset or drink they called October. Emerson.
occidentals: Western Christians of the Latin rite. See Orientals. Shipley.
octopus: A genus of eight-armed cephalopods, including numerous species, some of them of large size. See Devilfish,
octopetalous: Having eight petals or flower leaves.
octangular: Having eight angles; eight-angled. -- Oc*tan"gu*lar*ness, n.
occiput: 1. (Anat.) The back, or posterior, part of the head or skull; the region of the occipital bone. 2. (Zoöl.) A plate which forms the back part of the head of insects.
occasionally: In an occasional manner; on occasion; at times, as convenience requires or opportunity offers; not regularly. Stewart. The one, Wolsey, directly his subject by birth; the other, his subject occasionally by his preferment. Fuller.
occipitoaxial: Of or pertaining to the occipital bone and second vertebra, or axis.
occasionable: Capable of being occasioned or caused. Barrow.
octagon: 1. (Geom.) A plane figure of eight sides and eight angles. 2. Any structure (as a fortification) or place with eight sides or angles. Regular octagon, one in which the sides are all equal, and the angles also are all equal.
ocular: 1. Depending on, or perceived by, the eye; received by actual sight; personally seeing or having seen; as, ocular proof. Shak. Thomas was an ocular witness of Christ's death. South. 2. | The eyepiece of an optical instrument, as of a telescope or microscope.
ocellus: (a) A little eye; a minute simple eye found in many invertebrates. (b) An eyelike spot of color, as those on the tail of the peacock.
oculo: A combining form from L. oculus the eye.
ochre: (a) A impure earthy ore of iron or a ferruginous clay, usually red (hematite) or yellow (limonite), -- used as a pigment in making paints, etc. The name is also applied to clays of other colors. (b) A metallic oxide occurring in earthy form; as, tungstic ocher or tungstite.
octavo: A book composed of sheets each of which is folded into eight leaves; hence, indicating more or less definitely a size of book so made; -- usually written 8vo or 8º. | Having eight leaves to a sheet; as, an octavo form, book, leaf, size, etc.
octapla: A portion of the Old Testament prepared by Origen in the 3d century, containing the Hebrew text and seven Greek versions of it, arranged in eight parallel columns.
oca: A Peruvian name for certain species of Oxalis (O. crenata, and O. tuberosa) which bear edible tubers.
octodecimo: Having eighteen leaves to a sheet; as, an octodecimo form, book, leaf, size, etc. | A book composed of sheets each of which is folded into eighteen leaves; hence; indicating more or less definitely a size of book, whose sheets are so folded; -- usually written 18mo or 18º, and…
occasionate: To occasion. (old) The lowest may occasionate much ill. Dr. H. More.
occision: A killing; the act of killing. (old) Sir M. Hale.
ochlocratic: Of or pertaining to ochlocracy; having the form or character of an ochlocracy; mobocratic. -- Och`lo*crat"ic*al*ly, adv.
octostichous: In eight vertical ranks, as leaves on a stem.
occur: 1. To meet; to clash. (old) The resistance of the bodies they occur with. Bentley. 2. To go in order to meet; to make reply. (old) I must occur to one specious objection. Bentley. 3. To meet one's eye; to be found or met with; to present itself; to offer; to appear; to happen; to take place; as, I will write if opportunity occurs.
octostyle: Having eight columns in the front; -- said of a temple or portico. The Parthenon is octostyle, but most large Greek temples are hexastele. See Hexastyle. -- n. An octostyle portico or temple.
octad: An atom or radical which has a valence of eight, or is octavalent.
occupation: 1. The act or process of occupying or taking possession; actual possession and control; the state of being occupied; a holding or keeping; tenure; use; as, the occupation of lands by a tenant. 2. That which occupies or engages the time and attention; the principal business of one's life; vocation; employment; calling; trade. Absence of occupation is not rest. Cowper.
occlusion: 1. The act of occluding, or the state of being occluded. Constriction and occlusion of the orifice. Howell. 2. (Med.) The transient approximation of the edges of a natural opening; imperforation. Dunglison. Occlusion of gases (Chem. & Physics), the phenomenon of absorbing gases, as exhibited by platinum, palladium, iron, or charcoal;
oculary: Of or pertaining to the eye; ocular; optic; as, oculary medicines. Holland.
octodont: Of or pertaining to the Octodontidæ, a family of rodents which includes the coypu, and many other South American species.
occupier: 1. One who occupies, or has possession. 2. One who follows an employment; hence, a tradesman. (old) "Merchants and occupiers." Holland. The occupiers of thy merchandise. Ezek. xxvii. 27.
occecation: The act of making blind, or the state of being blind. "This inward occecation." Bp. Hall.
octonaphthene: A colorless liquid hydrocarbon of the octylene series, occurring in Caucasian petroleum.
oculina: A genus of tropical corals, usually branched, and having a very volid texture.
octofid: Cleft or separated into eight segments, as a calyx.
